display.purpose: Wordmark and every page <h1> (LoginPage, RegisterPage, ProfilePage) — self-hosted via @fontsource/space-grotesk imports in src/main.tsx, weights 500/600/700.

body.purpose: Post content, bio, comments, form labels, buttons — self-hosted via @fontsource/inter imports in src/main.tsx, weights 400/500/600.

chrome.purpose: Timestamps and metadata (text-xs, font-mono applied to numeric counts via TickingCount's tabular-nums, not a separate typeface).

shadows.name: shadow-card
shadows.purpose: Default elevation for every card: posts, composer, comment threads, auth forms. Neutral black, not accent-tinted, so ordinary content doesn't compete with primary actions.

shadows.name: shadow-glow
shadows.purpose: Elevation for gradient-filled primary controls (submit/follow/paylaş/gönder, liked state) — tinted from accent-strong so the primary action visibly 'lifts' toward the brand color. Removed entirely on disabled (disabled:shadow-none).

motion.name: tick
motion.purpose: Plays once whenever any count re-keys on change (likes, comments, follower/following/post stats) via TickingCount.tsx. Applied uniformly — no separate color-flash variant; the accent's reservation is carried by the like button's fill state, not by the number.

components.name: Primary Button (default)
components.description: Gradient-filled pill for submit/follow/paylaş/gönder — the app's one primary-action style.

components.name: Like Button (ghost / liked)
components.description: The one ghost control in the system that fills solid with the gradient — the single place where 'liked' and 'the brand accent' are the same visual event. Unliked state stays neutral border/text, hover swaps to accent.
components.css: .ds-btn-like { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; min-height: 44px; padding: 0 12px; border-radius: 9999px; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.09); background: transparent; color: #9d9ab0; font-size: 0.875rem; transition: border-color 0.15s, color 0.15s; } .ds-btn-like:hover { border-color: #9b82ff; color: #9b82ff; } .ds-btn-like--liked { border: none; background: linear-gradient(to right, #6845e8, #c92a72); color: #ffffff; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.4), 0 12px 28px -12px rgba(104,69,232,0.55); } .ds-tick { display: inline-block; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; animation: ds-tick 240ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); } @keyframes ds-tick { 0% { transform: scale(1.3); } 100% { transform: scale(1); } }

narrative.overview:
sosyal.log is a social feed for after the sun goes down — the app checked from bed, not from a desk under office light. This replaces an earlier "field notebook" direction (warm cream paper, ink-black text, monospace metadata) that read as flat and washed-out once actually lived in, and it deliberately goes further than the sibling Flask web client for the same backend, whose own design is a conventional light-first coral/teal card layout behind a manual dark-mode toggle: this client commits to dark as the default scene, not an opt-in.

Structure comes from layered near-black surfaces (never pure black, never a single flat gray), a self-hosted Space Grotesk display face for the wordmark and page headings against a self-hosted Inter body face, and one reserved accent — an indigo-violet-to-magenta gradient — spent only on primary actions, the liked state, and follow/submit buttons. Everything else stays neutral. Cards carry real depth: soft, color-tinted, offset-and-blurred shadows, not a flat outline or a bevel standing in for elevation.
keyCharacteristics: Layered dark surfaces (#0a0a10 ground → #14141c cards → #1c1c26 raised/disabled state), not a single flat charcoal
One reserved gradient accent (#6845e8 → #c92a72), spent only on primary actions, the liked state, and follow/submit — never on links or body text
Self-hosted Space Grotesk (display) + Inter (body), both via @fontsource imports in src/main.tsx — no system-font fallback used as a display voice
Real shadow depth (.shadow-card, .shadow-glow in src/index.css): offset, blurred, and — for the glow variant — tinted from the accent
Authored ring-and-glyph SVG marks for like/comment (src/components/icons.tsx), not emoji and not a generic icon library
Every count that changes scale-pulses once (.tick), applied uniformly

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: The gradient marks a primary action or the liked state and nothing else — never a link color, a focus ring, or a generic "success" signal. Comment controls and hover states stay neutral so the accent's rarity keeps its meaning.

rules.name: The Two-Shade Accent Rule
rules.body: The same hue never serves both "text on dark" and "white text on fill" — one shade is measurably too light for the former or too dark for the latter. accent (light) is for text/icons on the ground; accent-strong/accent-2 (deep) are for gradient fills only.

rules.name: The No Gradient Text Rule
rules.body: Emphasis comes from weight, size, or the wordmark's single accent-colored glyph (the "." in "sosyal.log") — never a bg-clip-text gradient fill on a text run. Verified absent from every bg-linear-to-r use in the build; all of them sit behind solid white or currentColor text, not behind transparent text.

dos: Do reserve the gradient for primary actions, the liked state, and follow/submit — everywhere else stays neutral ink/soft-text.
Do use accent (light) for text/links/icons on dark surfaces and accent-strong/accent-2 (deep) only for gradient fills behind white text — never swap the two roles.
Do keep every button, pill, and text input at min-h-11 (44px).
Do swap a disabled gradient button to a flat surface-2 fill with text-soft label — never dim the gradient with opacity.
Do give every card real offset-and-blurred shadow depth (shadow-card/shadow-glow), never a flat outline standing in for it.
donts: Don't put gradient text (bg-clip-text) anywhere — emphasis comes from weight, size, or a single solid-colored glyph.
Don't add a second display face; Space Grotesk is already self-hosted via src/main.tsx's @fontsource/space-grotesk imports.
Don't pull in a generic icon library or an emoji glyph for a new control; extend the ring-and-glyph pattern in icons.tsx.
Don't nest a card inside a card; post actions are pills on the card surface, not sub-cards.
Don't reach for a hard-edged block shadow — this world's depth is always soft and blurred, tinted from the accent only on primary actions.
